transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Hello! I'm Dora, and I've just completed your post-cataract surgery follow-up check. 

Do you have any questions about your surgery or your recovery?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, I do have a few questions. First, I was wondering when I can start doing a little bit of gardening?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Great question! You can start doing light gardening after 1 week following your surgery. 

However, you should avoid any strenuous or heavy exercise, and also avoid swimming for about a month.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Thank you for the information! I was also wondering when I can start using my eye gel for dry eyes?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
Good question! If you were using eye gel or drops for dry eyes before your operation, it's safe to continue using them unless you've been told otherwise by your doctor.

So you can go ahead and use it as you were before. If you're not sure about the specific instructions, just check with your GP or pharmacist.

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: That's helpful, thank you! I'm experiencing a lot of sensitivity to bright light. Is that normal after surgery?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.intended:
Some light sensitivity is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens, and wearing sunglasses when you're outside can really help with that.

However, if the light sensitivity is severe or your eye is also red and painful, that's not normal and we may need to check it further. 

Is the sensitivity mild, or are you experiencing significant pain and redness as well?
transcript.delivered: Some light sensitivity is normal as your eye adjusts to the new lens, and wearing sunglasses when you're outside can really help with that.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Should I still have some blurriness by now?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text:
It's quite common to have some blurriness in the first week after surgery, and it should improve quickly and settle down over time.

However, if your vision is still blurry or getting significantly worse, we may need to check it to make sure everything's okay.

How long has it been since your surgery?

Do you have any other questions?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: My surgery was a little over a week ago, so that explanation makes sense. Thank you for addressing all my concerns. I don't have any more questions right now.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: That's great! So just to confirm - have all your questions about your cataract surgery recovery been answered today?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes, they've all been answered. Thank you for your help!

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: You're very welcome! Take care, and best of luck with your recovery.
